title: Identity Theft Report and Affidavit Requirements by Claimant Identity Verification Pathway
content:
Requirements for identity theft documentation differ by Claimant Identity Verification pathway. Only one pathway requires a police or FTC report and the agency identity theft affidavit.

| Pathway | Police report or FTC IdentityTheft.gov report required | Agency identity theft affidavit required | Maximum age of the report at receipt (days) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Online Identity Proofing (IAL2) | no | no | 0 (no report required) |
| Video Trusted Referee Session | no | no | 0 (no report required) |
| In-Person Proofing — American Job Center | no | no | 0 (no report required) |
| In-Person Proofing — USPS Retail Location | no | no | 0 (no report required) |
| Documentary Verification by Mail | no | no | 0 (no report required) |
| Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification | yes | yes | 365 |

## Requirements on the Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification pathway

- **Report:** a police report or an FTC IdentityTheft.gov report — either one satisfies the report requirement.
- **Affidavit:** the agency identity theft affidavit, in addition to the report.
- **Age limit:** the report may be no more than 365 days old when it is received.

## Boundary illustration (hypothetical dates)

- A police report dated 365 days before the day it reaches the agency is within the age limit.
- A police report dated 366 days before the day it reaches the agency is older than the limit.
